report.summary: Chunk 4 of 5 for parse.py: implements split_generic, is_any_annotation, union_id, _decl_kind, _decorator_texts, _base_texts, _params_of, _alias_records, _end_line, _qual, and the _TypeWalk class with its methods. Contains docstring claims about generic splitting logic and enum base detection.
risks: split_generic | medium | The function uses _parse_expr which is defined elsewhere; its behavior is uncheckable. If _parse_expr returns None or unexpected nodes, split_generic may return incorrect results. | Verify _parse_expr handles all valid annotation strings and returns None for invalid ones.

_params_of | medium | The function assumes args.posonlyargs exists; if node.args is not an ast.arguments (e.g., lambda), it will raise AttributeError. The caller is expected to handle this, but no guard is present. | Confirm callers only pass ast.FunctionDef or ast.AsyncFunctionDef nodes.

_TypeWalk._class | low | The method appends to self.types, self.fields, etc., but these lists are never cleared; if the walker is reused, previous results accumulate. The __init__ resets them, so reuse is safe only if a new instance is created. | Ensure a new _TypeWalk instance is created per module.

_TypeWalk._assign | low | Only handles NewType assignments; other assignments like X = int are explicitly not treated as aliases. This may miss some type aliases defined via assignment. | Confirm that the intended design is to only capture NewType as alias.

handoff.purpose: Implement annotation splitting, declaration classification, and the recursive type walker.

symbols.name: split_generic
symbols.note: One-level generic split: returns (container, element_texts). Uses _parse_expr, _dotted_tail, _slice_elements. Cached with lru_cache.

symbols.name: is_any_annotation
symbols.note: Returns True if raw is bare Any/typing.Any, using normalize_annotation.

symbols.name: union_id
symbols.note: Returns stable group id for union site edges: f"{module}#{owner}:{role}:{param}".

symbols.name: _ENUM_BASES
symbols.note: Frozenset of known enum base class names.

symbols.name: _decl_kind
symbols.note: Classify a ClassDef into typeddict, namedtuple, enum, protocol, dataclass, or class. Base-derived kinds win over decorator-derived.

symbols.name: _decorator_texts
symbols.note: Extracts decorator texts from a node's decorator_list.

symbols.name: _base_texts
symbols.note: Extracts base class texts and keyword arguments from a node's bases and keywords.

symbols.name: _params_of
symbols.note: Returns parameters in reading order and the receiver candidate name.

symbols.name: _alias_records
symbols.note: Extracts AliasImport records from Import or ImportFrom nodes.

symbols.name: _end_line
symbols.note: Returns the end line number of a node, defaulting to start line.

symbols.name: _qual
symbols.note: Joins parts and name with dot.

symbols.name: _TypeWalk
symbols.note: Recursive type walker over statements with scope stack. Contains methods _class, _function, _self_target, _annassign, _assign.

claims.text: One level of generic: ``(container spelling, element texts)``.
claims.why: The function returns a tuple of (container, tuple of element texts).

The example depends on _parse_expr and _dotted_tail; the code path for list (in _SEQ_CONTAINERS) returns tail and filtered elts. Without knowing _parse_expr's output, we cannot verify the exact string.

claims.text: ``dict[str, User]`` -> ``("dict", ("User",))`` because a mapping's KEY is not its element
claims.why: The code for _MAP_CONTAINERS with len(elts) >= 2 returns tail and annotation_text(elts[-1]), which is the last element (value type).
For tail in _CALLABLE_NAMES, returns tail and annotation_text(elts[-1]) if elts non-empty.
If node is not ast.Subscript, returns ("", (text,)) where text is annotation_text(node).

claims.text: an unknown generic is ``("", ("MyGeneric[int]",))`` -- no container, because we refuse to guess that an unrecognised subscript is a container at all.
claims.why: If tail not in recognized containers, returns ("", (text,)) where text is annotation_text(node) of the full subscript.

claims.text: True for a bare ``Any``/``typing.Any`` -- the sentinel a caller must refuse to edge to. ``dict[str, Any]`` is NOT bare Any; it is a dict whose element type is unknown, which is a different fact and a different number.
claims.why: The function delegates to normalize_annotation(raw).is_any, which is defined elsewhere. The claim about dict[str, Any] not being bare Any is a semantic claim that cannot be verified from this code alone.

claims.text: Stable group id shared by every member edge of ONE union SITE. Derived entirely from the site's identity, never from a counter over a set or dict.
claims.why: The function returns f"{module}#{owner}:{role}:{param}" which is deterministic and based only on the inputs.

claims.text: Base-derived kinds win over decorator-derived ones, because a base changes what the declaration IS (a TypedDict is a dict shape, an Enum's members are values) while ``@dataclass`` only changes what is generated for it.
claims.why: The function checks bases first (TypedDict, NamedTuple, enum, Protocol) and only then checks decorators for dataclass. If a base matches, decorators are not considered.

claims.text: Fixed order, so the answer never depends on dict order.
claims.why: The checks are in a fixed sequence of if-elif-elif-elif-else, not iterating over a dict.

claims.text: Parameters in reading order, plus the receiver candidate name.
claims.why: The function processes positional args, vararg, keyword-only args, kwarg in order, and returns the first positional arg name as receiver candidate.

observations.what: split_generic uses _parse_expr which is not defined in this chunk; its behavior is assumed correct.
_params_of accesses args.posonlyargs without checking if it exists; if node.args is not ast.arguments, it will raise AttributeError.
The _TypeWalk class accumulates results in instance lists; if reused without re-initialization, results from previous walks persist.
_alias_records ignores potential syntax errors in node.names (e.g., no lineno attribute).
The _TypeWalk._assign method only handles NewType assignments; other type alias patterns (e.g., X = int) are intentionally not captured.
